# cuteafd-eval

> Results-first public ledger: two inference engines by tpurtell (CuteAFD and tpurtell's vLLM fork) serving GLM-5.3-Flash EXL3
> quantizations on one machine (2x NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Max-Q). Maintained by Michael M (UrbanAstroLA).

Every page is generated from the files in the repository; numbers are never typed into pages. Start with the
machine-readable files below rather than scraping HTML.

## Machine-readable entry points
- https://urbanastrola.github.io/cuteafd-eval/findings.json: the claims of the Thinking length investigation (TL-*) and of the CuteAFD v5 context probe
  (CP-*), one entry per claim, with status, value,
  95% interval, a JSON pointer into the source file, and the per-reply data and script that recompute it.
- https://github.com/UrbanAstroLA/cuteafd-eval/tree/main/results: one folder per run. In each: RUN.json (id, kind, title, protocol, engine,
  checkpoints), SUMMARY.json (every number its page shows), MANIFEST.json (sha256 of every file), README.md.
- results/*/analysis/samples.csv: one row per reply (arm, prompt, seed, finish, reasoning tokens, decode speed, tests).
  The context probe's table has one row per request (arm, pass, item, family, length, seed, finish class, fields, correct);
  its reference checkpoint's rows are in analysis/samples-reference.csv (same columns), recomputed by analysis/reference.py;
  passes 3 and 4 of all four configurations are in analysis/samples-extension.csv (same columns), recomputed by analysis/fourpass.py.
- results/2026-11-10-context-probe/bf16ref/BF16REF.json: distance from the BF16 model of the four configurations, with the
  per-window figures its fidelity-set values and intervals are recomputed from.
- https://github.com/UrbanAstroLA/cuteafd-eval/blob/main/protocol/README.md: the frozen protocol; protocol/HASHES.json binds published files to it.

## How to read the results
- Run kinds: measurement (protocol frozen before the first request), exploratory (evidence, not a frozen comparison),
  check. A finding's status says which; post hoc numbers are labelled post hoc.
- Intervals are 95% bootstrap intervals over the unit named (prompts, questions, windows, items); "detected" means the interval
  excludes the null (1 for ratios, 0 for differences). Bootstrap seeds differ per run: see each run's protocol, or
  recompute.bootstrap in findings.json.
- "Finished" = finish_reason stop and not capped. Medians in TL-* entries are over finished replies; the medians on the v5 page
  (thinking length, speed) are over all replies. findings.json has a definitions block
  with every estimator used.
- findings.json pointers are RFC 6901: unescape ~1 to / and ~0 to ~ after splitting (some keys contain a slash).
- Context probe (CP-*): three arms on CuteAFD v5.0.0 that differ in the precision of the tensors outside the experts: anchor
  (BF16 core and BF16 output head, FP8 conversions off; a locally derived checkpoint; the reference, not a recommendation),
  hqa (BF16 q_b_proj and o_proj, rest of the core and the head K6) and compact (K6 core and head). K4 experts and one seed
  list in every arm. A request scores fields correct / fields, 0 if it did not finish with stop; differences are paired by item
  and named "b - a" (above 0 = b higher). Data length label 128k is the 127K-token rendering. The K4-Core-K6-HQA repository
  is no longer available on the hub (checked 2026-11-11); the runs used a local copy.
- Reference checkpoint exlr8-k4 (CP-reference-*): added after the three-arm results were read; two single-message passes and one
  scoring capture, then passes 3 and 4 under amendment 1. It is a different checkpoint from the three arms, not a setting of
  the same one: any difference from an arm is
  a whole-checkpoint difference and is not attributable to one component. Its intervals are post hoc.
- Amendment 2 to the context probe (protocol/AMENDMENT-2026-11-12.md) adds a fifth configuration, k325-fp8. Its runs were in
  progress when this file was built: no entry holds a measured figure for it; CP-bits-per-weight holds its file accounting.
- Amendment 1 to the context probe (protocol/AMENDMENT-2026-11-11.md in the run folder) added single-message passes 3 and 4 per
  configuration; complete 2026-11-12 (CP-fourpass-*, CP-extension-pending). It was written after the two-pass results were read and
  before the first added request: the frozen rule applied to four passes, an extension, not the frozen comparison. The two-pass
  entries stay as the frozen protocol's result; the three pair entries and the two reference entries carry a dated note. Pass
  sets: p12 = passes 1-2, p34 = passes 3-4 alone, p1234 = all four. No correction for the number of intervals: one interval is
  not evidence on its own.
- Distance from the BF16 model (CP-bf16-*): the four configurations scored against the unquantized BF16 model on two reference
  sets that reach 14.4K tokens, so the 64K and 127K task lengths have no BF16 reference. Fidelity set: coarse KL (the reference's
  top 1,024 token ids plus the rest), ratio of sums over generated positions, window bootstrap. Teacher panel: full-vocabulary KL,
  mean over rows. The two measures are not comparable with each other. The official FP8 model and K3.25 figures quoted beside
  them come from other measurements and were not measured in that stage.
- Thinking-length ratios put K4-Core-K6, or the part under test, first: above 1 = it thought longer. Each finding states
  its own direction.
- Numbers from different model families or tokenizers are not comparable; NLL is per tokenizer.
- "BF16 core" means different things on the two engines: BF16 matrices on the vLLM fork, BF16 converted to FP8 at load on
  CuteAFD v4.0.0. The vLLM fork runs with a local loader modification, not a tpurtell release; derived checkpoints are
  local builds, not producer releases.

## Validate
- `python3 tools/verify.py` checks every manifest hash, every site link and anchor, every findings.json pointer, and
  recomputes the code-study ratios and test counts and the context-probe differences from the per-reply tables, and the
  context probe's fidelity-set distances from BF16 (values and intervals) from the per-window figures.
- Each run folder's code/ and analysis/ hold the scripts that produced its numbers; repro/REPRODUCE.md covers re-running.

## Status vocabulary in findings.json
- measurement: frozen rule: protocol and decision rule frozen (hashes in the run's protocol/FROZEN.json) before the first request
- measurement: post hoc: computed from frozen-run data after the run; not part of any decision rule
- measurement: descriptive: counted from frozen-run data; not part of any decision rule
- exploratory: run kind exploratory: useful evidence, not a frozen comparison
- source reading: read in source code and logs, no measurement
- judgement: source and measurements: a conclusion drawn from source reading and published measurements together; not isolated by a run of its own
- measurement: extension: passes added by a dated amendment, written after the frozen result was read and before the first added request; the frozen rule applied to more passes; not the frozen comparison
- measurement: planned descriptive: plan and file hashes written before the first request of the stage, after earlier results were read; descriptive, with no gate and no decision rule
- accounting: checkpoint files: counted from the headers of the checkpoint files; no model is run and nothing is compared by a rule

## Findings (summary)
- TL-code-vllm-core [measurement: frozen rule]: On the vLLM fork, does K4-Core-K6's 6-bit core change how long code replies think, against the original BF16 core? No: 1.00x [0.96, 1.04], not detected.
- TL-code-cuteafd-core [measurement: frozen rule]: On CuteAFD v4.0.0, does the native 6-bit core change how long code replies think, against the BF16 core converted to FP8 at load? Yes: 1.26x [1.24, 1.29], detected, every prompt above 1. See TL-code-engines and TL-code-fp8-arm for which arm differs and TL-fp8-ablation for which FP8 setting carries it.
- TL-code-engines [measurement: frozen rule]: Do the two engines agree on the core's effect on code thinking length? No: vLLM ratio / CuteAFD ratio = 0.79 [0.75, 0.83] (exp of the vLLM log ratio minus the CuteAFD log ratio, paired by prompt). By the reading stated before the run, the CuteAFD gap goes with how CuteAFD serves the core, not with the weight values.
- TL-code-fp8-arm [measurement: post hoc]: Which of the four code configurations thinks differently? CuteAFD's BF16-core configuration (core, KDA projections, vocabulary head and prefill activations in FP8): 0.82x the vLLM BF16 core on the 12 new prompts (0.78x over all 16), shorter on every prompt; the other three sit within about 4% of each other.
- TL-code-tests [measurement: descriptive]: Does the length difference change the result on code? Not between the two cores on either engine: CuteAFD 6-bit 50 and FP8-from-BF16 49 of 64; vLLM fork 6-bit 53 of 64 and BF16 58 of 63 finished; paired intervals include 0. Post hoc across all arms: TL-code-pass-pairs.
- TL-fp8-path [source reading]: What differs between CuteAFD's two core formats besides the core's weights? With a BF16 core, CuteAFD v4.0.0's launcher also puts the KDA projections (including three gate projections outside the core) and the vocabulary head in FP8, and prefill runs the MLA and MLP projections with FP8 activations; with the native 6-bit core these stay on the 6-bit kernels or in BF16. On a two-GPU head split the FP8 KDA path also comes with KDA output sharding, which v4 accepts only with FP8 KDA and clears for the native core. These are the launcher's defaults (its comment at run-family.sh:2337-2351, v4.0.0), with the author's stated reasons: decode speed and pool size, and output sharding to avoid rounding the GPUs' partial outputs, checked on teacher-forced top-1 and KL. The model notes (docs/models/glm5_flash.md 'Default precision') and the --kda-fp8 option text (mod.rs:189-197) describe BF16 KDA as the two-GPU default; the documents differ, and the launcher's choice is what runs.
- TL-fp8-ablation [measurement: frozen rule]: Which part of CuteAFD's FP8 path goes with the shorter code reasoning of the BF16-core checkpoint (local derived checkpoint, not a producer release)? The KDA launch setting: switching the KDA projections from FP8 to BF16 (on this two-GPU layout that also turns off KDA output sharding, which v4 runs only with FP8 KDA) gives 1.31x [1.24, 1.38], detected, every prompt above 1; then the vocabulary head 1.02x [0.97, 1.07] and prefill activations 0.99x [0.97, 1.02], not detected. With the KDA setting off the gap to the native 6-bit core closes (C-K6 / F-kda 0.96x [0.92, 1.01]); KDA's share of the gap 1.16 [0.95, 1.37] (above 1 = the point estimate passes the native core; the interval includes 1, consistent with the whole gap). Settings were switched off cumulatively.
- TL-code-pass-pairs [measurement: post hoc]: Across the code-thinking arms of both engines, does passing all hidden tests differ in paired replies? Post hoc, every contrast looked at (13): the arms with CuteAFD's FP8 settings switched off (F-kda, F-head, F-pre) and the vLLM BF16 core pass more often than both CuteAFD code-study arms; 5 of 13 intervals exclude 0, all that way, and 2 after allowing for 13 looks (F-pre, all three settings off, against each code-study arm). The two CuteAFD cores, a fifth apart in reasoning length, pass equally often: passing does not follow length, and the native core (none of the FP8 settings) passes about as often as the FP8-from-BF16 core.
- TL-fp8-where [judgement: source and measurements]: Where in CuteAFD does the code-length difference arise: prefill or generation? Most likely on the generation path (decode and speculative verify); prefill is not excluded. Prompts are 1,155-1,758 tokens against medians of 50-68K reasoning tokens; speculative verify steps run on the decode programs, which read the FP8 KDA copies, and KDA output sharding is not limited to prefill. The KDA setting also changes the KDA projections in prefill, and the prompt's recurrent state seeds every later token. Not separated: KDA in prefill against generation, plain decode against speculative verify.
- TL-experts [measurement: frozen rule]: Do the routed experts change thinking length? No measurable contribution: 0.99x [0.93, 1.05].
- TL-stop-cuteafd [exploratory]: On CuteAFD, does the core change when the model decides to stop on fixed science-question reasoning traces? No: -0.0144 [-0.0497, +0.0187] on the new questions; no effect on the earlier 11 either.
- TL-stop-vllm [exploratory]: On the vLLM fork, does the core change when the model decides to stop on fixed science-question reasoning traces? No: -0.0109 [-0.0315, +0.0046] on the new questions.
- TL-qbo [exploratory]: Do q_b and the output projections in BF16 move the stop decision? Not in general: +0.0118 on the 11 questions they were found on, -0.0032 [-0.0161, +0.0064] on 30 new questions, not replicated.
- TL-identity [measurement: frozen rule]: Do two launches of the same model agree? CuteAFD: bit-identical on every scored row, also two days later. vLLM fork: no; the launch difference is as large as the core's.
- CP-hqa-vs-anchor [measurement: frozen rule]: On CuteAFD v5.0.0, does the default HQA core (BF16 q_b_proj and o_proj, rest K6) score lower than a BF16 core on graded tasks from 4K to 127K tokens? 0.000 [-0.012, +0.012] in field score, pooled over lengths; the interval includes 0. No difference measured. Basis: 60 items at four lengths, two passes; strength: moderate (one model family, synthetic tasks). Per-length intervals at 64K and 127K are wider (see SUMMARY.json).
- CP-compact-vs-anchor [measurement: frozen rule]: On CuteAFD v5.0.0, does the K6 core (ATTENTION_MODE=compact) score lower than a BF16 core on the same tasks? -0.010 [-0.026, +0.006] in field score, pooled over lengths; the interval includes 0. No difference measured; compact's largest nominal gap is running totals at 64K and 127K (CP-ledger-long-context).
- CP-hqa-vs-compact [measurement: frozen rule]: Do the two modes of the K4-Core-K6-HQA checkpoint, hqa and compact, differ on the same tasks? +0.010 [-0.005, +0.025] in field score, pooled over lengths; the interval includes 0. No difference measured.
- CP-length-effect [measurement: descriptive]: Does accuracy fall with context length, and does core precision produce the fall? It falls in every arm, the BF16 reference included: field score 0.98 at 4K and 0.89 to 0.91 at 127K. The reference loses about as much as the other arms (0.08 against 0.07 and 0.09), so core precision does not produce it. A third to a half of the loss is replies that did not finish (cap or repetition abort, scored 0): among finished replies the 127K score is anchor 0.942, hqa 0.936, compact 0.928. Where the rest sits is open: the arms share the model, the K4 experts, the engine, the drafter, the sampling settings and the reply cap.
- CP-ledger-long-context [measurement: post hoc]: Does the K6 core cost accuracy on running totals (ledger tasks) at 64K and 127K? Open. compact - anchor is -0.062 [-0.127, +0.002] in field score (includes 0) and -0.138 [-0.263, -0.025] in every-field-right (excludes 0), on 20 items. Post hoc: 48 such intervals were computed and two exclude 0, both compact - anchor on ledger every-field-right (single message; with the eight-turn pass): a lead, not a finding. hqa - anchor on the same slice is -0.023 [-0.073, +0.023] in field score (includes 0).
- CP-turns-scope [measurement: descriptive]: Did the eight-turn pass test a conversation whose history the model wrote? No. Decode ran in every reply, but the model's own turns were a median 9% of the final prompt at 4K and 0.3-0.4% at 127K: at long context over 99% of the history was written by prefill. What the pass shows is split delivery: delivering the same input as eight messages shows no accuracy cost (16K to 127K: every interval includes 0, a cost up to about 0.07 is not excluded; 4K: eight turns score slightly higher in anchor and hqa, intervals exclude 0). The turn design is to be revised.
- CP-intermediate-caps [measurement: descriptive]: In the eight-turn pass, how often was a delivery turn's reply not the requested acknowledgement, and how often did it run to its 4,096-token cap? Not the bare acknowledgement: anchor 4, hqa 6, compact 17 turns. Ran to the cap: anchor 0 of 1920 turns (0 sessions); hqa 2 of 1920 turns (2 sessions); compact 13 of 1920 turns (8 sessions). 6 of compact's capped turns were in one session. Descriptive; the final answers were scored as usual.
- CP-kv-pool [source reading]: On two RTX PRO 6000, do the cheaper core settings admit a larger KV pool than the BF16 core? Not in the graded runs: every arm was admitted the configured maximum, 2,097,152 tokens, in all nine serving launches. The saving shows as resident weights and unallocated memory under the cap. A smaller pool for anchor was seen only in the scoring launches of the exploratory depth profile (16 requests at once).
- CP-exploratory-checks [exploratory]: What did the checks before the graded runs show? Depth profile (five arms: anchor, hqa, compact, fp8c = ATTENTION_MODE=fp8-compact, core-fp8 = the BF16-core checkpoint with the engine's default FP8 conversions; texts to 128K, not the task items): no arm measurably worse than the BF16 reference at predicting the text at any depth. GLM5_FLASH_FP8_PREFILL=off on the HQA checkpoint: every recorded distribution bit-identical, so not an arm. Two launches of the same arm: bit-identical rows. Prefix-cache resume against a decode replay: bit-identical in 45 of 46 conversations over four arms together (the exception is a harness artifact). Greedy output alone and eight at once: one text in all 260 requests per arm. One capture each; numbers are in the protocol text only.
- CP-reference-exlr8-k4 [measurement: post hoc]: How does a native EXLR8 K4 checkpoint of the same model, served by the same engine, score on the same graded tasks from 4K to 127K tokens? No difference measured from anchor or hqa: +0.006 [-0.007, +0.019] against anchor and +0.006 [-0.008, +0.019] against hqa. Against compact its field score is higher post hoc: +0.016 [+0.004, +0.029] over four lengths, +0.030 [+0.006, +0.056] at 64K and 127K pooled, +0.002 [-0.006, +0.009] at 4K and 16K. That is a lead, not a finding: the checkpoint was added after the results were read, and this is one of 84 intervals computed without correction, of which 3 exclude 0 (all exlr8-k4 - compact on field score). It is on the partial-credit score only: on every field right the pair does not separate (+0.025 [-0.017, +0.065]). exlr8-k4 is a different checkpoint from the three probe arms, not a setting of the same one. Any difference from a probe arm is a whole-checkpoint difference and is not attributable to one component. Basis: two single-message passes, 60 items, 480 requests per arm, 0 errors, prompt tokens equal to anchor's on every request; strength: low for the difference from compact (post hoc, one of many intervals), moderate for the absence of a measured difference from anchor and hqa (one model family, synthetic tasks, intervals of about 0.013 either side).
- CP-reference-capture [exploratory]: With the engine scoring given texts instead of generating, does the EXLR8 K4 reference checkpoint predict the text worse than the three probe arms, and how far apart are the arms? Not measurably worse at predicting the text: over the whole capture the most likely token is the given one as often as for anchor (-0.0007 [-0.0037, +0.0023] on the prefill path; the interval spans 0 on both paths); values by depth band are published without intervals. Its mean NLL is lower than anchor's (-0.0134 [-0.0199, -0.0070] nats, prefill path), which is not read as an improvement: 99 of 9,728 positions carry -91.48 of the -130.40 nat (70% of the sum), the median per-position difference is 0 and the arm is ahead on fewer than half of the positions. This capture does not measure distance from the unquantized BF16 model; that distance was measured afterwards for these four configurations, on two reference sets that reach 14.4K (CP-bf16-distance, added 2026-11-12). Between arms, which is not a distance from the BF16 model: the three probe arms share their experts, so the distance between two of them reflects the settings outside the experts alone, the core and for anchor the output head (prefill path, median KL 0.0004 to 0.0006, most likely token different on 4.20% to 5.15% of positions); exlr8-k4 has its own experts, so its distance to any probe arm (0.0015 to 0.0017; 8.83% to 8.88%) includes both expert quantizations and does not rank it against the probe arms by closeness to the BF16 model. exlr8-k4 is a different checkpoint from the three probe arms, not a setting of the same one. Any difference from a probe arm is a whole-checkpoint difference and is not attributable to one component. Basis: one capture per arm, five texts (not the task items), assistant frame; strength: low (exploratory, one capture, no correction for the number of comparisons).
- CP-fourpass-hqa-vs-anchor [measurement: extension]: Over four single-message passes, does the default HQA core (BF16 q_b_proj and o_proj, rest K6) score lower than a BF16 core on graded tasks from 4K to 127K tokens? No difference measured, and the bound is tighter than at two passes: +0.003 [-0.005, +0.012] in field score over four lengths (interval includes 0); the 95% interval reaches down to -0.005. The same reading in both pass sets: 0.000 [-0.012, +0.012] at passes 1-2 and +0.006 [-0.010, +0.021] at passes 3-4 alone. Basis: four passes, 60 items, 960 requests per arm, 0 errors; strength: the best-supported reading of this run (both pass sets; distance from BF16 not larger on either reference set, CP-bf16-distance); limits: one model family, one engine release, synthetic tasks.
- CP-fourpass-compact-127k [measurement: extension]: Over four single-message passes, does the K6 core (ATTENTION_MODE=compact) cost accuracy, and where? Indicated, not established. compact is the lowest arm in both pass sets (four lengths, four passes: 0.946 against 0.955 to 0.959), and the gap is at 127K: 0.887 against 0.918 to 0.924; up to 64K it is level with the others. hqa - compact: +0.037 [+0.004, +0.073] at 127K and +0.013 [+0.002, +0.024] over four lengths (both exclude 0; over four lengths the interval excludes 0 only at four passes, in neither pass set alone). compact - anchor: -0.031 [-0.070, +0.008] at 127K and -0.010 [-0.021, +0.002] over four lengths (both include 0), so hqa and compact separate from each other while neither separates from anchor. Basis of the strength: the same sign in both pass sets and, at 127K, in every pass against hqa (hqa 0.929, 0.896, 0.927, 0.946; compact 0.885, 0.894, 0.892, 0.877) and in three of four against anchor (0.875, 0.931, 0.923, 0.942; pass 1 reverses); not one interval among 102, of which 6 exclude 0 at four passes where about 5 would with no difference anywhere. These counts alone do not settle where the gap comes from. Pooled over four passes it matches the unfinished replies (14 of 240 at 127K against 7, 5, 4; finished replies score 0.942 against 0.936 to 0.945), but the two pass sets do not agree on that split: in passes 1-2 compact had as many unfinished replies at 127K as anchor (5 and 5) and a lower finished-only score (0.928 against 0.942); in passes 3-4 it had 9 unfinished against 2, 2, 3 and the highest finished-only score (0.956). Of its 18 unfinished replies over all lengths, 15 reached the reply cap and 3 ended on the repetition abort. A scoring capture on given texts to 128K, which samples nothing, shows no deficit for compact at predicting text (NLL minus anchor's -0.0055 [-0.0109, -0.0004], lower is better; exploratory, one capture). The capture scores given text and does not locate the gap, which was seen in generated replies at 127K. The 127K length lies beyond the 14.4K reach of both BF16 reference sets, so the BF16 stage (CP-bf16-distance) neither supports nor contradicts this. Added 2026-11-12, after this entry was first published: the replies themselves were read (CP-fourpass-endings). The gap is join replies at 127K that did not finish, not answers that were wrong; whether the K6 projections raise the rate of that ending is indicated, not established.
- CP-fourpass-exlr8-k4 [measurement: extension]: Did the two-pass lead of the EXLR8 K4 reference checkpoint over compact repeat, and where does that checkpoint sit over four passes? The lead did not repeat. exlr8-k4 - compact was +0.016 [+0.004, +0.029] at passes 1-2 (interval excluded 0, post hoc); passes 3-4 alone give +0.002 [-0.017, +0.022] and the four-pass interval includes 0 (+0.009 [-0.003, +0.021]). At 127K the four-pass difference is +0.033 [-0.002, +0.069], the same size as hqa's over compact (+0.037 [+0.004, +0.073]). On score exlr8-k4 sits with anchor and hqa (-0.001 [-0.012, +0.009] and -0.004 [-0.016, +0.007]). It has fewer replies fully right than those two in count: 738 of 960 against 760 and 768 (compact 739). Over four lengths those two intervals include 0 (-0.023 [-0.054, +0.008] and -0.031 [-0.067, +0.002], as a share of replies); at 64K and 127K pooled the one against anchor excludes 0 (-0.046 [-0.087, -0.004]), one of the 6 among 102. On ledger at 64K and 127K it has 48 of 160 fully right against 68, 59, 59 (anchor, hqa, compact). exlr8-k4 is a different checkpoint from the three probe arms, not a setting of the same one. Any difference from a probe arm is a whole-checkpoint difference and is not attributable to one component.
- CP-bf16-distance [measurement: planned descriptive]: How far are the four configurations from the unquantized BF16 model, and how much of that distance lies in what differs between the probe arms? All four sit in one band. Fidelity set (coarse KL from BF16, generated positions, contexts to 14.4K): hqa 0.0302 [0.0255, 0.0344], compact 0.0314 [0.0263, 0.0359], anchor 0.0328 [0.0275, 0.0377], exlr8-k4 0.0360 [0.0300, 0.0416]; that is 1.4 to 1.7 times the baseline the engine author recorded in the fidelity set's manifest for the official FP8 model (0.0216; quoted, not recomputed here) and 0.62 to 0.74 of a K3.25 Core-FP8 checkpoint measured on CuteAFD v3.0.1 on 2026-10-26 (0.0484; teacher panel 0.0476); both are rows from other measurements, for scale. Teacher panel (full-vocabulary KL, 2K contexts): anchor 0.0320 [0.0241, 0.0419], hqa 0.0316 [0.0238, 0.0410], compact 0.0297 [0.0236, 0.0364], exlr8-k4 0.0305 [0.0244, 0.0374]. The two sets use different measures and are not comparable with each other. What differs between the three probe arms is a small part of the distance: they share their K4 experts and differ by at most 0.0026 on the fidelity set, under a tenth of the total. The plan stated in advance that anchor's distance would not be zero (quantized experts and the engine's numerics; the two are not separated here). anchor is also not the closest: hqa - anchor is -0.0026 [-0.0042, -0.0011] on the fidelity set (interval excludes 0; hqa closer) and -0.0004 [-0.0014, +0.0006] on the teacher panel (includes 0). anchor differs from hqa in its output head as well as its core (both BF16 in anchor, which is launched with the engine's three FP8 conversion settings off; as logged, KDA FP8 reads Off in every serving launch of the three probe arms and the FP8 prefill setting reads none in anchor and [Mla, Ffn] in hqa and compact) and is a locally derived checkpoint; why it measures slightly farther than hqa on one set is an open question (added 2026-11-12). exlr8-k4 is 0.003 to 0.006 farther than each probe arm on the fidelity set (intervals exclude 0) and level with them on the teacher panel. The two sets place it differently and this stage does not say which is nearer. The fidelity set is the engine author's; its relation to the calibration data of either checkpoint is not known. The teacher panel is drawn from the corpus the producer of the K4 experts published and can favour the experts the three probe arms carry (stated in the plan before the first request); a tilt of that kind would run toward the probe arms. exlr8-k4 is a different checkpoint from the three probe arms, not a setting of the same one. Any difference from a probe arm is a whole-checkpoint difference and is not attributable to one component. 30 intervals are listed (24 fidelity set, 6 teacher panel), 13 exclude 0, all on the fidelity set; none was selected. Neither set reaches past 14.4K: the 64K and 127K lengths of the task runs have no BF16 reference here, so the one task difference indicated in this run (CP-fourpass-compact-127k) lies beyond both sets. Basis: one launch per arm plus an exact repeat (CP-bf16-repeat), two reference sets. Limits: one engine build, one checkpoint revision per arm, prefill path only, contexts to 14.4K; descriptive, with no gate and no ranking rule, and the two sets do not order the four configurations the same way.
- CP-bf16-repeat [measurement: planned descriptive]: Does a second launch reproduce the BF16-distance result, and does the float64 port used for the intervals agree with the engine's own scorer? Yes, exactly. A second launch of each of the four configurations gave a KL difference of 0.0 on the fidelity set and the same most likely token on 15,104 of 15,104 generated positions. The float64 port agrees with the engine CLI's own per-record output on 32,768 of 32,768 records per configuration and launch (largest KL difference 0.0). All four pass the engine CLI's own fidelity gate on the fidelity set (KL at most 0.05, top-1 at least 0.93). The overall fidelity-set values and intervals of CP-bf16-distance are recomputed by tools/verify.py from the published per-window figures. Limits: one engine build, prefill path only.
- CP-extension-pending [measurement: extension]: Do two further single-message passes per arm change the reading? In part. The passes are complete (ran 2026-11-11 17:02 to 2026-11-12 03:59; 1,920 added requests, 0 errors); this entry keeps its id from the time they were pending. hqa against anchor: unchanged, with a tighter bound (CP-fourpass-hqa-vs-anchor). compact: a cost at 127K is indicated, not established, and hqa - compact excludes 0 at four passes while neither separates from anchor (CP-fourpass-compact-127k). The two-pass lead of exlr8-k4 over compact did not repeat (CP-fourpass-exlr8-k4). Paired intervals narrowed to 0.71 to 0.75 of their two-pass half-width for the three probe pairs and 0.79 to 0.90 for pairs with exlr8-k4. Intervals excluding 0 of 102 per pass set: 4 at passes 1-2, 13 at passes 3-4 alone, 6 at four passes; about 5 would with no difference anywhere, and no correction is applied.
- CP-fourpass-endings [measurement: post hoc]: How did the replies of the four single-message passes end, and what is compact's lower score at 127K made of? 44 of 3,840 replies did not finish (anchor 9, hqa 9, compact 18, exlr8-k4 8), none of them with answer text, so each scores 0 under the frozen rule whatever its reasoning had reached. compact's excess is in one place, the join family at 127K: 10 of 80 replies unfinished against anchor 4, hqa 2, exlr8-k4 1; every unfinished join reply of the run is at 127K. ledger is level (anchor 5, hqa 7, compact 7, exlr8-k4 7 over all lengths) and trace has 1 in total. The 127K difference in score is that family: hqa - compact +0.037, of which join +0.035; anchor - compact +0.031, of which join +0.027. The finished join replies at 127K score level (0.989 to 0.997 over the four configurations). The ending is one every configuration shows, the BF16-core anchor included: in 15 of the 17 unfinished join replies at least half of the reasoning is the prompt's records copied out in order, and in the 16 of them with a copy run all eight of the item's correct identifiers (13 replies) or seven of them (3) occur in the reasoning before the run starts (a text match). Whether the K6 q_b_proj and o_proj raise the rate of that ending is indicated, not established: the paired difference in the share of unfinished join replies at 127K is +0.100 [+0.025, +0.175] for compact - hqa (excludes 0) and +0.075 [-0.013, +0.163] for compact - anchor (includes 0), and by pass compact had 1, 2, 4, 3 and anchor 3, 1, 0, 0, so passes 1-2 alone show no excess. Read with CP-fourpass-compact-127k: the gap there is replies that did not finish, not answers that were wrong. Not measured: a larger reply cap, other sampling settings, a limit on reasoning length, natural documents. Limits: post hoc; 20 items per family; the thresholds for copying (share of at least 0.5) and for a copy run (20 lines) were chosen after the replies were seen (the 44 unfinished replies are listed with their shares, so another threshold can be applied); reply text is not published, only the derived per-reply counts.
- CP-bits-per-weight [accounting: checkpoint files]: In one unit, how large is each configuration's checkpoint compared with the unquantized BF16 model, and where do the configurations differ? Bits per weight (stored bits / weights; BF16 = 16), language model as stored: anchor 4.35 (27.2% of BF16, 162.3 GiB); hqa 4.17 (26.1% of BF16, 155.8 GiB); compact 4.10 (25.6% of BF16, 153.2 GiB); exlr8-k4 4.08 (25.5% of BF16, 152.2 GiB); k325-fp8 3.55 (22.2% of BF16, 132.7 GiB). At BF16 the same weights are 597.5 GiB. The routed experts are 94.9% of the weights and sit at 4.00 to 4.01 bits in the four configurations with K4 experts, so their whole-model figures lie close together; k325-fp8 is the one that changes the experts (3.26 bits, three quarters of the expert matrices at 3 bits and one quarter at 4). Outside the routed experts the figures spread: anchor 16.00, hqa 9.66, compact 7.25, exlr8-k4 6.55, k325-fp8 13.65 (exlr8-k4 is lowest there: 4-bit trellis on o_proj, q_b_proj, the shared experts and the dense feed-forward, FP8 on the embedding, the head and the other attention projections). hqa to compact moves 0.67% of the weights (o_proj and q_b_proj of the main layers) from 16 bits to 6, 2.6 GiB of files, 0.1 GiB of it the same two projections in the multi-token-prediction block; anchor to compact moves 2.4%, 9.1 GiB. hqa and compact are one checkpoint that stores those two projections twice; each configuration counts the copy its setting loads. Bits per weight is a size, not a quality score: among the four measured configurations neither distance from BF16 (CP-bf16-distance) nor task score follows it. As stored is not as run: under the engine's defaults the load line of k325-fp8 reports its attention group held as FP8, converted at load, and an FP8 output head, so part of what its files hold at BF16 runs at FP8; an as-run figure is not computed because the logs do not itemize the conversion by matrix. k325-fp8 is a fifth configuration added on 2026-11-12 (protocol/AMENDMENT-2026-11-12.md); this entry holds its file accounting only, and its task passes and BF16-reference capture were running when this was written. Limits: file accounting, not memory in use and not arithmetic precision at run time; the vision tower is not counted (every configuration ran with vision off); whether the engine uses the multi-token-prediction block when serving was not checked.

## Runs (results/<id>/RUN.json)
- 2026-10-26-cuteafd-setup-checks (check): Core-FP8 expert bytes and FP8 projections checked against K3.25-v1; CuteAFD source audit
- 2026-10-26-cuteafd-vs-vllm (measurement): CuteAFD v3.0.1 vs tpurtell's vLLM fork v0.9.2: precision, throughput, long output
- 2026-10-26-e1-router-route (exploratory): CuteAFD router logits across its 160/161-row route switch (one GPU, one kernel)
- 2026-10-27-k4-vllm-cuteafd (measurement): K4 (brandonmusic GLM-5.3-Flash-tr3-4bpw) on tpurtell's vLLM fork v0.9.2 and CuteAFD v3.0.1: precision, throughput, long output
- 2026-10-27-long-context-pilot (exploratory): Needle retrieval at 256K, 512K and 1M tokens, both engines, K3.25 (one request per prompt and engine)
- 2026-10-27-vllm-startup-cache (measurement): vLLM v0.9.2 startup time with and without persisted JIT caches, and CuteAFD's for comparison
- 2026-10-30-cuteafd-v4 (measurement): CuteAFD v4.0.0 against tpurtell's vLLM fork v0.9.2 on K3.25 and K4, and K4-Core-K6 on CuteAFD v4.0.0
- 2026-11-02-thinking-length (measurement): Thinking length and the 6-bit core of K4-Core-K6: BF16 core-tensor swaps on fixed traces (G2) and in free generation (G4), with loop checks
- 2026-11-02-tool-calling (measurement): Multi-turn tool calling (tool-eval-bench, 88 scenarios): CuteAFD v4.0.0 and the vLLM fork v0.9.2 on K3.25 and K4, CuteAFD on K4-Core-K6
- 2026-11-03-cuteafd-core-swap (measurement): CuteAFD core swap: K4-Core-K6's 6-bit core against its BF16 core (same experts) and against K4, in free generation and on fixed traces
- 2026-11-05-attn-position (exploratory): Does the core's effect grow with position? Position analysis of the fixed-trace dumps, and the vLLM fork with q_b and the output projections in BF16 together
- 2026-11-05-code-thinking (measurement): Code thinking length on CuteAFD: K4-Core-K6's 6-bit core against its BF16 core, 16 code prompts x 4 seeds
- 2026-11-06-cuteafd-fp8-ablation (measurement): Which part of CuteAFD's FP8 path shortens code reasoning: KDA FP8, FP8 head and FP8 prefill switched off cumulatively
- 2026-11-06-new-questions (exploratory): New questions: the q_b + output-projection stop-decision shift and the core, on 30 questions not used before
- 2026-11-06-vllm-code-thinking (measurement): Code thinking length on the vLLM fork: K4-Core-K6's 6-bit core against its BF16 core, 16 code prompts x 4 seeds
- 2026-11-10-context-probe (measurement): CuteAFD v5.0.0 core precision at long context: BF16 reference, HQA and K6 core on graded tasks from 4K to 127K tokens
